name: Notre-Dame de la Garde
_about: NOTRE-DAME DE LA GARDE, Marseille (Esperandieu, 1853-64), the Romanesque-Byzantine basilica on the summit fort, on its OSM plan (church, tower, dome, statue, terrace, steps, lift building, retaining walls) and Wikipedia's dimensions: the UPPER CHURCH -- a nave of three square bays under cupolas on pendentives between transverse arches, three side chapels a side (their twin windows), the crossing under the DOME on an octagonal drum (a window under a gable in every face, 32 ribs, the cross), transept fronts of two windows and a rose, the choir's barrel and the APSE's half dome over five blind arcades on red granite columns, the sacristies; the 41 m TOWER before it (the porch and the bronze doors, two stages of blind arcades, the belfry on red colonnettes with its bourdon, the terrace with balustrade and four angels, the round CAMPANILE of sixteen columns and the gilt VIRGIN AND CHILD, 11 m, on it), its octagonal stair turret; the CRYPT in the rock (barrel nave, six chapels, the altar and the Vierge au Bouquet, Mazenod and Pius IX in its narthex, the stairs up to the sacristies); the whole in courses of white Calissanne and green Golfolina stone, inside red and white marble, mosaics in gold. THE FORT: the terrace walked round the church, the porch terrace, the bastion's platform and the DRAWBRIDGE over the ditch, the two flights up from it, the stair pier and the LIFT tower, the double staircase from the road, the lower east terrace and its flights, the fort's ranges (tools/archgen/notre_dame_garde.py).

rock._about: the rock the church stands on, its top the crypt's floor (the crypt is cut into the summit of the hill)

crypt vault._about: the crypt's low barrel vault, cut in the rock: from the tower's foot to the apse

crypt east wall._about: the crypt's nave walls: an arch into each of its six chapels

crypt east transept back._about: the door from the crypt's transept to the stair up to the sacristy

crypt altar._about: the crypt's high altar in Golfolina stone

vierge au bouquet pedestal._about: the pedestal of the Vierge au Bouquet behind the crypt's altar

crypt founders pedestals._about: Ramus's marble statues in the crypt's entrance: Mgr de Mazenod, who founded the basilica, and Pius IX

crypt portal._about: the crypt's door straight ahead from the drawbridge, in the bastion's face under the porch terrace

east sacristy stair._about: the stair from the crypt up to the sacristy, beside the choir

church floor._about: the upper church's floor, over the crypt

east outer wall._about: the church's outer walls in white and green courses: the chapels' twin windows (the nave's light), the transept's front of two windows and a rose; the cornice

east frieze._about: the pierced frieze along the wall heads, hiding the low roofs

east pilasters._about: the pilaster strips along the outer walls at the transverse arches

east sacristy wall._about: the sacristies' outer walls, their doors onto the terrace

nave east wall._about: the nave's walls: an arch into each side chapel, the lunettes of the cupolas' arches over them

transverse arch 1._about: the transverse arches between the nave's bays, in courses of red and white marble

nave pendentives._about: the pendentives of the nave's three bays

nave cupolas._about: the three cupolas over the nave, gold mosaic inside (doves round a fleuron)

crossing front arch._about: the crossing's four great arches on its piers

east transept vault._about: the barrels over the transept arms

crossing pendentives._about: the crossing's pendentives (the four evangelists in mosaic)

dome._about: the dome over the crossing: the octagonal drum, a window under a gable in every face, the ribbed dome in white and green courses (OSM: 45 m to the cross)

drum base._about: the square base round the drum's foot, over the roofs

drum pinnacles._about: small pinnacles at the drum's corners

dome cross._about: the gilt cross over the dome

choir east wall._about: the choir's walls, a door through each into the sacristy

apse wall._about: the apse's outer wall, behind the arcades

apse columns._about: the red granite columns between the apse's arcades

apse half dome._about: the apse's half dome: the ship in a medallion amid vine scrolls and birds on gold

apse dome band._about: the mosaic band at the half dome's springing (AVE MARIA GRATIA PLENA)

high altar._about: the high altar in marble and gilt bronze

nave roof._about: the nave's low roof behind the frieze

transept roofs._about: the transepts' gabled roofs, their gables over the fronts

narthex._about: the porch in the tower's foot, behind the bronze doors

nave._about: the nave up into its cupolas

drum interior._about: inside the drum (its ring, its window reveals)

tower._about: the bell tower, 41 m over the terrace, in white and green courses: the porch (the bronze doors; the crypt's way under it), two stages, the belfry

tower arcade front 1._about: the blind arcades of the tower's two stages: five arches a face, the middle one round its window

tower balconies._about: the small balconies under the middle windows

belfry columns._about: the belfry's colonnettes of red granite and pink sandstone between its openings

bourdon._about: Marie-Josephine, the bourdon (8.2 t), hung in the belfry

tower terrace._about: the terrace on the tower, round the campanile's foot

tower balustrade front._about: the pierced balustrade round the tower's terrace

campanile plinth._about: the campanile (12.5 m): a round core within sixteen columns, its cap, the pedestal of the statue

campanile columns._about: the campanile's sixteen columns in red granite

statue pedestal._about: the round pedestal of the Virgin

bonne mere._about: La Bonne Mere: the Virgin and Child in gilt copper by Lequesne (11.2 m, 1870) over the campanile, the Child on her left arm blessing the city

tower stair._about: the octagonal stair turret against the tower's south-west face: from the terrace (its door to the west) to the tower's terrace

tower stair bridge._about: the step from the turret's belvedere onto the tower's terrace

summit terrace 1._about: the summit terrace round the basilica on the old fort's rock, walked all round the church

porch terrace 1._about: the porch terrace before the tower, over the crypt's passage

platform._about: the drawbridge's platform at the bastion's head, before the crypt's door

drawbridge gate._about: the gate the drawbridge drops from

east flight._about: the two flights from the drawbridge's platform up to the porch terrace on either side, the crypt's door between them

east bartizan._about: the bartizans at the bastion's corners

drawbridge._about: the drawbridge over the ditch, timber on iron

pier flight._about: the stair pier in the ditch: from the double staircase's landing up to the drawbridge

lift tower._about: the lift tower (1892) in the ditch: its door at the road and its door at the top onto the drawbridge's pier

lift._about: the lift: from the road to the drawbridge's pier (index.html: a stair's shortcut)

stair landing._about: the landing of the double staircase, on the counterscarp

east road flight._about: the double staircase from the road: two flights of 34 steps meeting on the landing

east terrace._about: the lower terrace east of the basilica, on the fort's casemates

east flight north._about: the flights from the lower east terrace up to the summit

west range._about: the fort's ranges beside the summit: the old barracks on the west, the casemates on the east -- plain stone under tiled hipped roofs
